title: Pager suppression intent scoring and automated decision flow
creator: Asha Kapoor
content:
Summary:

We need an automated, intent-scoring based pager suppression and decision flow to reduce noisy pages while preserving fast response for genuine user-impacting SLO breaches. This ticket defines the scoring model, suppression windows, circuit-breaker tie-ins, multi-region failover triggers, and the on-call automation runbook that can act (suppress, escalate, or trigger failover/load-shed) when thresholds are met. The goal is to reduce noisy wakeups by ~40-60% in non-critical degradations while preserving median detection/mitigation time for P0 incidents.

Why this work matters:
- Current pager volume causes on-call fatigue: frequent transient errors and cascaded infra alerts spur immediate pages even when automatic mitigation is possible.
- We have seen multiple incidents where premature paging prevented automated regional failover/safe-load-shed from completing.
- Reducing noise improves MTTR and on-call focus for real degradations; it also enables staged automatic responses (circuit breakers/load shedding) to improve overall user experience under partial outages.

Scope / Acceptance Criteria:
- Implement an alert intent-scoring layer upstream of paging that consumes signals (SLO breach severity, sustained error rate, regression delta, region, service owner calendar, recent deploy flag, related incident markers) and outputs a numeric score [0-100].
- Suppression rules: scores < 30 => suppress page, create ticket only; scores in [30-60) => page to secondary on-call with 10-minute cooling window; scores >= 60 => page primary immediately.
- Integrate scoring with circuit-breaker policy: if service-level error-rate upper bound breaches for >60s and score >=40, automatically trip local circuit-breaker and attempt partial load-shed before paging primary.
- Multi-region failover automation: if primary region latency p95 > SLO AND secondary region healthy AND score >=75, trigger automated canary failover plan (DNS weight shift 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 5m steps) with automatic rollback if error rate increases.
- Runbook artifact created and stored in Confluence with step-by-step operator actions and automated playbook triggers wired into PagerDuty and our orchestration engine.
- Metric dashboard panels and alerts updated: noise-rate, suppressed-pages, avg MTTR for suppressed vs paged incidents, false-suppression rate < 5% after 2-week canary.

Design decisions & rationale:
1) Scoring model inputs (initial):
   - SLO breach severity (binary: minor/major) weighted by 30
   - Trend delta (30s/5m) weighted by 20
   - Region health spread (other regions) weighted by 15
   - Recent deploy flag (last 30m) negative weight -10
   - Ticket/incident ancestry (ongoing incident) positive weight +10
   - Anomaly confidence (ML classifier from metrics) weighted 15
   Rationale: SLO severity and trend matter most; deploys indicate possible expected noise so reduce immediate pages.

2) Score thresholds chosen to favor safety early in rollout. We can relax after monitored canary.

3) Human-in-the-loop for first month: suppressed high-confidence events will notify a secondary digest Slack channel (#ops-suppressed) every 3m with actions suggested.

Implementation Plan (tasks):
- Spike (done): small prototype that computes score from AlertManager webhook + metrics in Prometheus (completed 2026-02-18). See spike notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Pager+Intent+Spike
- Library: create intent-scoring microservice that exposes /score endpoint (Node service). Code PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-score/pull/12 (in review).
- Integration: wire scoring step into Alert -> Pager pipeline in AlertRouter; implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alert-router/pull/237 (draft).
- Automation: extend orchestrator with actions: trip-cb, start-load-shed, initiate-failover. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/401
- Runbook authoring: Confluence page draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Intent+Score+Runbook
- Dashboard: Grafana dashboard panel PR: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/intent-score-dashboard (panel 7, 8 added).

On-call Runbook (operator-facing) — canonical steps:
1) Alert received -> check score badge on alert. If score <30, no paging occurred; open suppressed digest and review logs. If artifact silent, mark ticket as triaged.
2) score 30-59: secondary on-call receives page. Secondary runs quick triage: check p95, errors/sec, recent deploys, and region health dashboard. If automated CB/load-shed already started, observe for 5m; if recovery, close. If not, escalate to primary.
3) score >=60: primary paged. Follow emergency runbook: check rollback, region failover eligibility, and traffic steering controls.
4) Automated circuit-breaker response: if orchestrator tripped CB, confirm list of degraded endpoints and which clients are being shed. Decide whether to expand load-shed or open manual failover.
5) Failover procedure (automated canary then escalation): monitor secondary telemetry at 30s resolution; if error rate stable and latency <= SLO, continue weight shift; otherwise auto-rollback to 0 and page SRE.
6) Post-incident: capture decision timestamp, score, whether automation acted, manual interventions, and include in incident ticket.

Telemetry & Queries (initial examples):
- Prometheus alert condition (SLO breach simplified):
  sum(rate(request_errors_total[1m])) / sum(rate(request_total[1m])) > 0.05 and histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) > 0.5
- Noise metric: suppressed_pages_total / total_pages_total over 7d window.
- False suppression check: label: suppressed=true AND incident_acknowledged_within_5m=true -> flag for manual review.

Rollout plan & safety gates:
- Canary (region us-west-2): enable scoring but only suppress pages for scores <25 and send digest to #ops-suppressed. Monitor false-suppression rate for 7 days.
- Phase 2 (50% of services): increase suppression threshold to 30, enable secondary paging window. Add multi-region failover triggers behind manual approval.
- Phase 3 (full): enable automated CB + load-shed with automated failover for a small set of non-critical services.
- Gate metrics: false-suppression rate <5%; suppressed-targeted incidents resolved automatically in >60% cases within 10m; no increase in customer-visible errors.

Risk & Mitigations:
- Risk: over-suppression of legitimate P0 incidents. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, secondary digest, immediate manual escalation path, and fast rollback for failover.
- Risk: automation mis-triggers during deploys. Mitigation: deploy window flag lowers score automatically; require score bump for critical actions during deploy windows.

Testing plan:
- Synthetic load tests: inject error spikes and measured score outputs; verify automations behave as expected.
- Chaos tests: simulate region partition and ensure circuit-breaker, load-shed and failover behave.
- On-call dry runs: schedule blue-team exercises to validate runbook clarity.

Progress updates (timeline):
- 2026-02-10: Ticket created (Asha Kapoor).
- 2026-02-12: Spike kickoff, identified basic feature set and scoring inputs.
- 2026-02-18: Prototype scoring service and Prometheus adapter (spike complete).
- 2026-02-25: Initial integration into AlertRouter (end-to-end test in staging).
- 2026-03-01: Grafana panels created and sent for design feedback.
- 2026-03-05: PRs opened for orchestrator actions (pull requests linked above).
- 2026-03-10: Security review triage completed for orchestration PR; no secrets or new auth surfaces introduced.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How should we encode operator schedules (on-call hours, holidays) into score calculation? Proposal: pull from PagerDuty API as a normalized feature (assigned_oncall boolean).
- Should we surface score reasoning (which signals contributed) in the alert UI? Proposed yes; prototype shows top-3 contributing signals. UX spike scheduled (PM + Design).
- Do we want an ML-based recalibration service over time? Long term yes; initial plan uses deterministic weighted features with telemetry-based reweighting.

Post-deployment measurement plan:
- Weekly review of suppressed vs paged incident ratios in reliability guild meeting.
- 30-day retrospective to evaluate missed pages (if any) and adjust weights.
- Instrumentation: store score and contributing signals as labels on incident ticket for future model building.

Next steps (short-term):
- Merge ops-score PR and deploy to staging (Ethan).
- Complete AlertRouter integration and add feature flags (Noor).
- Draft Confluence runbook to replace this ticket text with canonical operator steps (Asha + Priya).

If you want to test the scoring logic manually, run the staging scoring endpoint against these example payloads:
- High confidence outage: {"slo_severity": "major", "error_rate": 0.12, "recent_deploy": false, "region_health": "degraded"} -> expect score >= 75.
- Transient spike after deploy: {"slo_severity": "minor", "error_rate": 0.03, "recent_deploy": true, "region_health": "healthy"} -> expect score < 30.
